verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly has a first-party docs page, "Decision making with Bayesian statistics," in its experimentation section. That page describes how results identify a leading or winning variation, so a documented Bayesian engine stands behind experiment results. However, the pack has no evidence of variance-reduction options, which the story explicitly requires, and the statistics are evidenced only through a page title and one sentence. Missing for 10: variance-reduction options (e.g., CUPED/covariate adjustment), detail on the statistical methodology, any frequentist option, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can trust a documented statistics engine (Bayesian or frequentist, with variance-reduction options) behind experiment results

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly highlights the leading variation when there is not yet enough experiment data to declare a winning variation.
Experiments let you measure the effect of features on end users by tracking metrics your team cares about.
